title: A first-year plan
summary: An example of a first year in Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting, step by step: from a taster session to your first competitions. It also shows when to make each big purchase.

body.html: Below is an example plan, not a fixed scheme. Everyone moves at their own pace, and gun laws differ between countries. The idea is to spend money once you know what you need.

Step 1. A taster session. Find a ground with a coach and try Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting with the ground's gun. Glasses and hearing protection are often lent. You do not need to buy anything yet.

Step 2. A few lessons with a coach. Regular sessions in the first months: safety, stance, the gun mount and your master eye, the eye your brain relies on, so the gun points where that eye looks. Now it is worth buying your own safety glasses and hearing protection: they cost little, matter a lot, and your own fit better.

Step 3. Club and documents. If you enjoy shooting, join a club and ask about federation membership, a sports licence and insurance. If your country requires a firearms permit, start applying now: it can take a long time.

Step 4. Gun fit and your own gun. Once you train regularly, have a gun fitting with a coach or a gun fitter. Then buy a gun, new or used and checked by a gunsmith. Add a slip or case, a cleaning kit and a safe if the law requires one.
Step 5. Vest and small items. A shooting vest, a cap, comfortable shoes and a cartridge bag, once it is clear how and where you shoot.

Step 6. First competitions. Start with club shoots close to home: a small entry fee, familiar faces, a calm atmosphere. Keep a diary of training and results; if a competition is on ClayArena, your results appear there too (How to find your results and your profile). Later you can try bigger competitions. ClayAway training tours are also being prepared.

key_points.html: First a taster session, with no purchases.
Your first own items: glasses and hearing protection.
Buy a gun after regular training and a gun fitting.
First competitions: club shoots close to home.

did_you_know.html: In many countries the law requires a gun to be kept in a safe or a locked cabinet, so plan for one in the budget together with the gun.
